title: Patch: Mythics arrive in full art, Prismatic is full art, and Legendaries default to Extended art
notes: Default looks by rarity (R3343000): the registry marks a variant's first level as a card rarity's default look (defaultOn), which the Default variant draws, a token by its printed rarity: Full art's first level on every Mythic and Extended art's on every Legendary. Every account owns it there with no ledger row, it is offered there nowhere (a pick, a token or the Chase Shard bar naming it is a 400, and no roll, pack or dev fill places it), and its variant's ladder starts at the level above it, next with nothing owned; rows held before stay and still count. A Mythic's Default prints full art while the Full-art cards setting is on and its normal face otherwise; a Legendary's prints Extended art, its words kept, and keeps its window on the board (R3343001). Prismatic's first level adds the full-art frame, so both its levels print full art, chrome across the face and never gold, and a Radiant face keeps every mark (R2725004). The Collection names and pictures a Mythic's and a Legendary's Default by that look and lists the ladders from the level above it (R3343002). How cards look only: nothing plays differently.

player.title: Mythics arrive in full art
changes: Every Mythic card now shows in full art by default, its picture across the whole card. Turn off Full-art cards in the settings to see its text instead.
Every Legendary card now shows in Extended art by default, its picture running past its window behind the card's text.
Prismatic is now a full art at both its levels: the chrome picture covers the whole card.
On a Mythic, Full art now starts at its animated level, and on a Legendary, Extended art at its animated level: you can earn those next with nothing else owned.
If you already owned Full art on a Mythic or Extended art on a Legendary, you keep it. Radiant cards keep their gold frame and marks under every look.
